assumptions.note: Average isolated yield per step. Overall yield is this raised to the number of steps, which is why step count dominates everything downstream.
Process mass intensity contributed by one step at 100% yield — solvents, reagents, water, work-up. Divided by overall yield to give the route's PMI.
Blended cost of everything that goes in, at 10 kg scale: building blocks, reagents, solvent, and its disposal. Scaled for smaller campaigns by procurement_scale_exponent.
Fully loaded cost of one person-day in a kilo-lab, including plant time, analytics and overhead. A CRO quote sits at the top of this range; an academic lab far below.
Charge, react, quench, work up, isolate. Purification is charged separately.
Crystallisation if you are lucky. Chromatography costs more and is charged a premium on top.
Kilo-lab batch size. More product means repeat batches, which is why cost per gram falls sub-linearly with scale.
Operator time for n batches goes as n^exponent: the second batch of the same step is quicker than the first.
Material cost per kg against scale. Buying 10× more material makes it modestly cheaper per kg.
Classical resolution throws away at least half the material and needs a separation; asymmetric catalysis trades that for catalyst cost.
Palladium-catalysed coupling: catalyst and ligand, plus metal scavenging and ICP-MS release testing.
Charged when the structure gives little hope of a crystalline intermediate: silica, solvent and time.
Densely halogenated or unusual-element cores must be bought rather than made, and often cannot be bought at all.
Immobilised enzyme consumed per kg of product in a biocatalytic step, assuming it is recycled a few times.
Screening a panel and, if needed, a round of directed evolution to make one step work on your substrate. Paid once, not per gram.
An enzymatic step that works tends to be high-yielding and selective, which is the point of using one.
Titre of a secondary metabolite in an engineered host after initial strain work. Orders of magnitude of headroom exist here, which is why the cost range is wide.
Working volume of the vessel assumed for a campaign.
Media, utilities, sterilisation, operators and QC for one fermentation, excluding recovery.
Fraction of the titre that survives extraction and purification to isolated compound.
Recovery and purification cost, as a fraction of the fermentation cost it follows.
Pathway assembly, host engineering and titre improvement to reach the assumed titre. Paid once.
Analytical release of the final batch: identity, assay, impurities, residual solvent and metals.
The quoted range is the point estimate divided and multiplied by this. It is deliberately wide: an uncalibrated model with a narrow error bar would be worse than no number at all.

agent.headline: Achiral 452 Da aryl piperazine amide: make it by convergent chemical synthesis, about $100/g (range $45–220) and about 18 weeks (range 10–32) to 1 kg.
agent.justification: The molecule has no stereocentres, no macrocycle and no enzyme-amenable motif. Chemical synthesis is the only route the rules consider, and no resolution or biocatalytic step is needed. The N-aryl piperazine bond is the forced operation: a Pd-catalysed Buchwald coupling, which adds a 1.18 cost premium plus palladium scavenging. The other key bond is the amide between the piperazine and the 2-methylsulfonyl-4-fluorobenzoic acid. The route is estimated at 6 steps with 26.2% overall yield and a PMI of 183 kg/kg. The tools give $100.07/g (low $45.49, high $220.16) and 18.0 weeks (low 10.0, high 32.4).
risks: Residual palladium after the Buchwald coupling must meet the metals specification on the final compound. A scavenger or crystallisation purge needs to be demonstrated.
The 4-benzylaniline-derived piperazine intermediates may not crystallise, which would force chromatography at kg scale and raise cost and PMI.

Amide coupling to the ortho-methylsulfonyl benzoic acid is sterically hindered. Activation may be sluggish, and the 4-fluoro group is open to SNAr side reactions with piperazine, giving regioisomeric impurities.
The 18-week estimate assumes no failed step and no repeat batch. Route scouting alone is 9.6 weeks, and one repeat would move the timeline toward the 32-week high case.

agent.headline: Achiral 495 Da diarylmethane–aryl piperazine amide is made by a roughly 6-step convergent chemical synthesis, about $100/g (range $45–220) and about 18 weeks (range 10–32) for 1 kg.
agent.justification: The molecule has no stereocentres, no macrocycle and no enzyme-amenable motifs, so the tools offer only chemical synthesis and it needs no resolution or biocatalysis. The aryl–piperazine C–N bond and the diarylmethane link force palladium-catalysed coupling (Buchwald or Suzuki-type), which adds a 1.18 cost factor and a metal specification. The final step would be an amide coupling of the piperazine with the 4-fluoro-2-(methylsulfonyl)benzoic acid fragment. The tools put the route at 26.2% overall yield and PMI 183 kg/kg. The docking score of -10.74 kcal/mol only explains why the molecule was shortlisted. It does not affect route choice, and it is not evidence of activity.
risks: Residual palladium on the final compound: the scavenging and crystallisation steps need to be shown to reach the clinical metal specification, and they may add a step.

The route is a heuristic step count with no retrosynthesis behind it. The 26.2% overall yield, and so the cost, could move toward the high end of $45–220/g if the coupling or the benzylic C–C bond formation underperforms.

The aryl fluoride ortho/para to the electron-withdrawing sulfone and carbonyl could undergo SNAr with the piperazine amine during amide formation or coupling, giving regioisomer or dimer impurities that need to be controlled.

The final API is a primary benzamide with a sulfone and is likely to have low solubility. Crystallisation and polymorph control, and purification without chromatography at kilogram scale, are not yet shown; a chromatography step would raise both cost and time.

agent.headline: Achiral 472 Da aryl piperazine amide: make it by conventional chemical synthesis, about $100/g point estimate (range $45–220) and 18 weeks (range 10–32) to 1 kg.
agent.justification: The molecule has no stereocentres, no macrocycle and no enzyme-amenable motif, and chemical synthesis is the only route the rules consider applicable. The decisive bond is the aryl–piperazine N–C bond to the diaryl ether, which forces a Pd-catalysed (Buchwald-type) coupling or an SNAr alternative. The route finishes with amide coupling to the 2-methylsulfonyl-4-fluorobenzoyl piece. With no resolution needed, the 6-step estimate is a short, convergent route. The tool figures are $100.07/g point (low $45.49, high $220.16), PMI 183 kg/kg and 26.2% overall yield. They include a 1.18 premium for the Pd coupling.
risks: Palladium carry-over: the Buchwald coupling needs a scavenging step and a metals specification on the final compound. Run a Pd-removal screen early and consider an SNAr or Ullmann alternative to avoid Pd.
The 6-step count is a heuristic, not a retrosynthesis. Route scouting could add steps or lower the 26.2% overall yield, which would push cost toward the high case of $220/g.
The timeline assumes one campaign with no failed step and no repeat batch. The high case is 32.4 weeks.

logP of 4.12 and a neutral, aromatic-rich structure may make the final API hard to crystallise or purge impurities from, which could force chromatography at kilogram scale. The tools did not model this.
